q-34364.name: Question 1
q-34364.problem:
The matrix $E$ and the vector $b$ are given below.
Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(E).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}\cdot {x}_{4}$, where ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, ${x}_{3}$, and ${x}_{4}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{e}_{1}+{x}_{2}{e}_{2}+{x}_{3}{e}_{3}+{x}_{4}{e}_{4},$ and ${e}_{1}$, ${e}_{2}$, ${e}_{3}$, and ${e}_{4}$ are respective columns of $E.$

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ 16 & -4 & 10 & 2 \\ 11 & -3 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
q-34364.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(E),$ we need to check if the equation $Ex=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[E\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[E\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 16 & -4 & 10 & 2 & -1 \\ 11 & -3 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -9 \\ 11 & -3 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}+{x}_{4}=4 \\ 0=-9 \\ 11{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-{x}_{4}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get a false statement $0=-9.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that $b\notin \text{Col}(E).$

q-35562.name: Question 2
q-35562.problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -7 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 4 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$
q-35562.worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ then the equation $Ax=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -7 & 7 \\ 1 & -4 & 4 \\ 3 & 5 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 4 \\ 2 & -7 & 7 \\ 3 & 5 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & 5 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 17 & k-12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-17){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & k+5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=4 \\ {x}_{2}=-1 \\ 0=k+5.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=k+5,$ which means that $k=-5.$

q-74210.name: Question 3
q-74210.problem: Consider the matrix given by $C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 5 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(C).$
q-74210.worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(C),$ then the equation $Cx=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[C\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ -3 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 6 \\ 2 & -4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & k-4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & k-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=2 \\ -4{x}_{2}=6 \\ 0=k-1.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=k-1,$ which means that $k=1.$

q-110978.name: Question 4
q-110978.problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 12 \\ k+30\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$
q-110978.worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ then the equation $Ax=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 1 & 12 \\ 0 & 5 & k+30\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 12 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & k+30\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 12 \\ 0 & 3 & 21 \\ 0 & 5 & k+30\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(\frac{1}{3}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 7 \\ 0 & 5 & k+30\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & k-5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=12 \\ {x}_{2}=7 \\ 0=k-5.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=k-5,$ which means that $k=5.$

q-111046.name: Question 5
q-111046.problem:
The matrix $D$ and the vector $b$ are given below.
Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(D).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}+{x}_{4}$, where ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, ${x}_{3}$, and ${x}_{4}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{d}_{1}+{x}_{2}{d}_{2}+{x}_{3}{d}_{3}+{x}_{4}{d}_{4},$ and ${d}_{1}$, ${d}_{2}$, ${d}_{3}$, and ${d}_{4}$ are respective columns of $D.$

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & 6 & 4 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 6 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 8 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
q-111046.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(D),$ we need to check if the equation $Dx=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[D\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[D\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & -2 & 6 & 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 6 & 5 & -1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 6 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 6 & 5 & -1 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}-2{x}_{4}=1 \\ 0=6 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}+{x}_{4}=-8 \\ {x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}-{x}_{4}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

From the  second equation, we get a false statement $0=6.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that $b\notin \text{Col}(D).$
